claim: Fragment certificate: verify(witness) (no imports, no I/O, plain-list witness, fail-closed raises, exact integer arithmetic) confirms for each p in {5, 17, 257, 65537} that p is a Fermat prime with p ≡ 2 mod 3, p ≡ 1 mod 4, (3/p) = -1, and 3 is a primitive root mod p — the concrete instance content of L1. The universal quantifier over all Fermat primes is not finitely checkable, so this is a fragment; L1 records the favorable subfamily closes neither branch.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
